content_voiceover: This slide bundles the myeloma vaccination schedule with anemia and cytopenia management. On vaccines, influenza is annual for everyone and publicly funded. Pneumococcal vaccination uses the sequential strategy: PCV13 first, one dose, then PPV23 at least one year later, though high-risk patients can shorten that gap to eight weeks; PPV23 itself can be repeated after five years, but public funding is generally limited to age sixty-five and up. Zoster vaccination is recommended for everyone, but only the non-live recombinant subunit vaccine, since these patients are immunocompromised, and it's self-pay. COVID-19 follows the rolling national guidance. For anemia, if a myeloma patient has symptomatic anemia with hemoglobin persistently under ten and no other identifiable cause, consider an erythropoiesis-stimulating agent, erythropoietin alfa forty thousand units weekly or erythropoietin beta thirty thousand units weekly, especially with concurrent renal impairment or low endogenous erythropoietin. Target hemoglobin should stay under twelve, and if there's no response after six to eight weeks, stop the ESA rather than escalating. Because anti-CD38 antibodies like daratumumab and isatuximab interfere with the indirect antiglobulin test and confound blood typing, get a type and screen before starting these drugs. Granulocyte colony-stimulating factor is used for neutropenia per standard practice, but thrombopoietin receptor agonists for myeloma-related thrombocytopenia aren't recommended yet given limited clinical data.
keypoints: Pneumococcal: PCV13 first, then PPV23 at least 1 year later (8 weeks if high-risk); repeat PPV23 at 5 years
Zoster vaccine must be non-live recombinant (immunocompromised patients); self-pay
ESA for symptomatic anemia with Hb under 10 and no other cause; target Hb under 12, stop if no response by 6-8 weeks
Type and antibody screen BEFORE anti-CD38 therapy, since daratumumab/isatuximab interfere with crossmatch
G-CSF standard for neutropenia; TPO receptor agonists not recommended for myeloma thrombocytopenia
keypoint_voiceover: Three testable points. Pneumococcal vaccination is sequential, PCV13 then PPV23 at least a year later, and zoster vaccine must be the non-live recombinant form because these patients are immunocompromised. For anemia, ESAs target hemoglobin under twelve and get stopped if there's no response by six to eight weeks. And always pull a type and antibody screen before starting anti-CD38 therapy, since daratumumab and isatuximab interfere with the indirect Coombs test.
